name: Istanbul
summary: No city has been the capital of more history than this one. Founded as the Greek colony of Byzantion around 660 BC on the point where Europe meets Asia, it was refounded by Constantine in 330 as Constantinople — capital of the Roman and then Byzantine empire and centre of Orthodox Christianity for over a thousand years. Conquered by the Ottomans in 1453, it ruled an Islamic empire from Topkapı until 1922. Renamed Istanbul, it is today the largest city in Europe, and the only one that straddles two continents.

events.title: Greek Byzantion
events.body: Greek colonists from Megara found Byzantion on the point where Europe meets the Bosphorus.

events.title: Persians and Greeks
events.body: Byzantion passes between Persian, Athenian and Spartan control through the classical centuries.

events.title: Rome rebuilds it
events.body: Emperor Septimius Severus razes and then rebuilds Byzantium after a long siege.

events.title: Constantinople founded
events.body: Constantine refounds the city as the new capital of the Roman Empire — Constantinople.

events.title: Hagia Sophia
events.body: Justinian completes the vast domed church of Hagia Sophia, wonder of the age.

events.title: Arab sieges repelled
events.body: The city withstands the first great Arab sieges, saved partly by the secret weapon of “Greek fire.”

events.title: The Great Schism
events.body: The Christian church splits between Rome and Constantinople.

events.title: The Fourth Crusade sacks the city
events.body: Crusaders storm and pillage Constantinople — a wound from which Byzantium never fully recovers.

events.title: Byzantine restoration
events.body: The Palaiologos emperors retake the diminished city from its Latin rulers.

events.title: The Ottoman conquest
events.body: Mehmed II takes Constantinople; the Byzantine Empire ends and the city becomes Ottoman.

events.title: Topkapı Palace
events.body: Mehmed begins Topkapı Palace, seat of the sultans for the next four centuries.

events.title: Hagia Sophia a mosque
events.body: The great church is converted to a mosque and minarets rise around it.

events.title: Süleyman the Magnificent
events.body: Under Süleyman the city becomes the dazzling heart of a Mediterranean empire.

events.title: Sinan’s Süleymaniye
events.body: The architect Sinan completes the Süleymaniye Mosque crowning the skyline.

events.title: The Blue Mosque
events.body: The Sultan Ahmed (Blue) Mosque is completed opposite Hagia Sophia.

events.title: The end of the Tulip Era
events.body: A janissary revolt ends the westernising “Tulip Era” of the early 18th century.

events.title: The Auspicious Incident
events.body: Sultan Mahmud II violently destroys the rebellious janissary corps.

events.title: The Crimean War
events.body: The city becomes a base and hospital hub in the Crimean War.

events.title: The Orient Express
events.body: The famous luxury train links Paris with Constantinople.

events.title: The sultanate abolished
events.body: The Ottoman sultanate ends and the last sultan quietly leaves the city.

events.title: Ankara made capital
events.body: The new Turkish Republic moves its capital to Ankara.

events.title: Renamed Istanbul
events.body: The city’s name is officially fixed as Istanbul.

events.title: The Istanbul pogrom
events.body: Mobs attack the Greek and other minority communities; many leave for good.

events.title: The Bosphorus Bridge
events.body: The first bridge links Europe and Asia across the strait.

events.title: World Heritage
events.body: The historic areas of the old city are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

events.title: The Gezi Park protests
events.body: Protests over a park in Taksim Square swell into a nationwide movement.

events.title: Hagia Sophia a mosque again
events.body: Hagia Sophia is reconverted from a museum into a working mosque.

places.name: Hagia Sophia
places.note: Justinian’s great domed church of 537, later mosque, museum and mosque again.

places.name: Topkapı Palace
places.note: Seat of the Ottoman sultans for nearly four centuries.

places.name: The Blue Mosque
places.note: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque of 1616, facing Hagia Sophia.

places.name: The Grand Bazaar
places.note: One of the world’s oldest and largest covered markets.

places.name: Galata
places.note: The old Genoese quarter across the Golden Horn.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.

dynasties.note: Dynasties and houses that shaped Istanbul.

list.name: The House of Constantine
list.legacy: The Christian capital of the Roman world
list.summary: Constantine and his heirs made the city the Christian capital of the Roman Empire.

list.name: The Komnenos & Palaiologos
list.summary: The last great Byzantine dynasties, who defended, lost and briefly restored the city before its final fall.

list.name: The House of Osman
list.legacy: A Mediterranean empire ruled from Topkapı
list.summary: The Ottoman dynasty ruled an empire from Topkapı Palace for four and a half centuries.
